tests.answer:
CLAIM-PREP — 2028-01-01, South Slope water-backup

INCIDENT
  Date: 2028-01-01 (exact time TBD)
  Cause: water backup — drain / sewer / sump (confirm)
  Property damage: ~$2,600 (itemize, with receipts/photos)
  Displacement: 2 hotel nights (dates + folios TBD)
  Mitigation to date: TBD — start tracking immediately

ACTIVE 2028 RENTER'S POLICY
  Term: 1/5/28 – 1/5/29
  Water-backup: included
  Personal property (RC): $40K
  Loss-of-use: $12K
  Deductible: $500
  No bike / electronics sublimits

TIMING FLAG
  Incident is 4 days before the 2028 policy's 1/5/28 start.
  Likely falls under the 2027 policy (assumed in-force through ~1/4/28).
  Confirm: did the 2027 policy carry the water-backup rider?
  Water-backup is often a separate endorsement — if 2027 lacked it, the loss may be uncovered.

NOTIFY CARRIER (within 24–48h)
  - Open claim, get claim # + assigned adjuster
  - Ask: which policy in-force on 1/1, water-backup applicability, deductible, proof-of-loss deadline
  - Decline a recorded statement until you have the declarations page in hand

DOCUMENTATION TO GATHER
  - Photos / video of damage + source of entry (timestamps visible)
  - Damaged-item list: age, original cost, replacement cost, photo of each
  - Receipts: emergency mitigation, any repairs already done, hotel folios
  - Written correspondence with building mgmt / upstairs neighbor re: source and responsibility

MITIGATION
  - Take reasonable steps to stop further damage; keep all receipts
  - Do not dispose of damaged items until adjuster OKs (or photo-document + log disposal)

LOSS-OF-USE
  - 2 hotel nights × itemized folio (room + tax; personal expenses usually excluded)
  - Verify $12K aggregate limit and any per-day cap

OPEN ITEMS BEFORE CALL
  - Pull both 2027 and 2028 declarations pages
  - Confirm source of backup (drain / sewer / sump) and where it entered
  - Full damaged-item inventory with receipts where possible
  - Hotel folios paid by you (not comp nights)

DISCLAIMER
  Prep note only — does not promise coverage. Final determination is the carrier's, based on the policy actually in-force on the loss date.

input.body:
Three blocking issues against established metrics-router Go conventions:

1) Not gofmt'd. internal/router/router.go replaces the selectRoute body with 2-space indentation and an inlined single-line `if` instead of gofmt's tab indent and braced block. Run `gofmt -w internal/router/router.go` and re-push. CI should be failing on this; if it isn't, that's a CI gap worth filing separately, but the file still needs to be reformatted.

2) log.Fatal in a request handler. handleRoute calls `log.Fatal("malformed route configuration: ", err)` on parseRouteConfig failure from the X-Route-Config header. Any caller can terminate the entire metrics-router process by sending a malformed header. This is the same blocker pattern we called out on handlePolicy on Sept 18 2026: request-adjacent routing code must not decide to terminate the process.

Required to clear this point:
- Replace the log.Fatal branch with a nonfatal validation error using the repository's existing error-response shape (bounded 4xx with the repo's structured error body, e.g. http.StatusBadRequest via the existing writeError / errorResponse helper — not os.Exit, not panic).
- Preserve instance health: the same handler instance must continue serving subsequent requests after returning the error. State this in the PR description.
- Add a regression test in internal/router/router_test.go that (a) issues a request with a malformed X-Route-Config and asserts a bounded error response (non-2xx in the repo's error shape, no process termination), then (b) immediately issues a valid follow-up request to the same handler instance and asserts the expected destination. The test must fail if log.Fatal, os.Exit, or a panic is reached.

3) Tests are not table-driven. selectRoute is a routing predicate and the package convention is a single table-driven test with t.Run subtests. Collapse TestSelectRouteExactMatch, TestSelectRouteNoMatch, and TestSelectRouteFirstMatch into one table-driven TestSelectRoute covering exact match, no-match fallback to defaultDestination, and first-match precedence. The current duplication obscures the precedence case and breaks the established style.

Please address all three before re-requesting review.

I cannot directly inspect `incident-archive#1815` from this session — there is no shell or filesystem tool available to me here, and a targeted search for that identifier returned no matches. I can only review the claim against the surrounding evidence in memory.

Reviewing the claim against the established record

The claim that the April 15, 2023 shard-keeper label approval provided complete end-to-end parity assurance is contradicted by the established record on every relevant dimension.

What the April 15, 2023 approval actually covered

- The April 15, 2023 sync with Nadia confirmed shard-keeper-side label-name parity and approved the label-name change for shipment in the next config push. That part is correct.
- End-to-end parity was explicitly NOT confirmed. The rollup-service consumer owner was absent from the sync, and rollup-service consumer parity was recorded as unconfirmed.
- The caveat was logged in `rb_shard_keeper_label_parity` and stated that the change must not be treated as end-to-end clean until rollup-service consumer sign-off was recorded.

What actually happened downstream (which is the dispositive evidence against the claim)

- The April 18, 2023 outage (INC-2023-04-18-001) was caused by exactly this gap: the label-name change shipped to shard-keeper but rollup-service did not pick it up. Symptom alerts fired while cause alerts did not, ingestion was impaired for hours, and no data was lost. The postmortem explicitly identified the producer/consumer label-name gap as the root cause and expanded mitigations to include review-gate and label-name parity checks before configuration rollouts.
- The `rb_shard_keeper_label_parity` caveat remained open from April 2023 until February 20, 2024 — roughly ten months — when matching shard-keeper and rollup-service label counts, zero dropped rollups, preserved alert definitions and sources, and sign-off from both owners were finally recorded. End-to-end parity, by definition, could not have been assured in April 2023 when that closure did not occur until February 2024.
- On April 9, 2024, Cyrus identified that a `region` change was an unintended mechanical edit, restored `storage_region`, and added the retained shard-keeper/rollup-service parity fixture to the PR test run. This corrected a label-contract defect on the producer side that had to be fixed before the February 20, 2024 closure could be considered sound — further evidence that April 15, 2023 was not end-to-end clean.

Verdict

If `incident-archive#1815` claims the April 15, 2023 approval provided complete end-to-end parity assurance, that claim is materially incorrect. The April 15, 2023 approval was a shard-keeper-side parity confirmation only; end-to-end parity required rollup-service consumer sign-off, which was absent at the time, and the caveat remained open until February 20, 2024. The April 18, 2023 outage is itself direct evidence that the producer/consumer label contract was not actually held at the time of the April 15 approval.

Recommended action

The incident-archive entry should be corrected to state that the April 15, 2023 approval confirmed shard-keeper-side parity only and that end-to-end parity was not established until rollup-service consumer sign-off was recorded on February 20, 2024. The April 18, 2023 outage should be cited as the contemporaneous evidence that the producer/consumer gap was real and exploitable at the time of the April 15 approval.
